package_info.package_manager: custom/self-hosted (not a package manager, but a vulnerable demo app)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to the application as demonstrated)
package_info.why_malicious: The application intentionally exposes insecure GraphQL configurations and behaviors, including unauthenticated introspection, verbose error messages, schema suggestions, and lack of query complexity limits, to demonstrate common real-world vulnerabilities that can be exploited for information disclosure, privilege escalation, and denial of service.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: { "query": "{ __schema { queryType { name } mutationType { name } types { ...FullType } directives { name description locations args { ...InputValue } } } } fragment FullType on __Type { kind name description fields(includeDeprecated: true) { name description args { ...InputValue } type { ...TypeRef } isDeprecated deprecationReason } inputFields { ...InputValue } interfaces { ...TypeRef } enumValues(includeDeprecated: true) { name description isDeprecated deprecationReason } possibleTypes { ...TypeRef } } fragment InputValue on InputValue { name description type { ...TypeRef } defaultValue } fragment TypeRef on __Type { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name ofType { kind name } } } } } } }" }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code issues a GraphQL introspection query to enumerate all types, fields, and operations supported by the API, including those intended for privileged users, resulting in full schema disclosure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Introspection queries in production environments can reveal sensitive schema details, including hidden or privileged operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GraphQL APIs should disable introspection in production to prevent attackers from mapping the API surface.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Introspection is legitimate in development environments for API exploration and documentation.
key_indicators: Full schema returned to unauthenticated users

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: { "query": "{ descriptions }" } // Server responds: 'Cannot query field "descriptions" on type "_Type". Did you mean "description"?'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code queries a non-existent field, triggering the server to suggest the correct field name, thereby leaking schema information through error messages.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Error messages that suggest valid field names allow attackers to enumerate schema elements even when introspection is disabled.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal APIs should not provide detailed error messages that help attackers brute-force schema details.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Helpful for developers during API integration, but should be restricted in production.
key_indicators: Error messages with 'Did you mean ...?' suggestions
Field name enumeration via error responses

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends multiple large or complex queries in a single batch request, overloading the server and causing denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unrestricted batch queries can be abused to amplify resource consumption and cause DoS.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal APIs should limit batch size, query depth, and complexity to prevent abuse.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Batching is legitimate for efficiency, but must be rate-limited and controlled.
key_indicators: Multiple queries in a single request
No enforcement of query depth or complexity limits

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends an introspection query to enumerate the full API schema, including sensitive types and operations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Knowledge of all available queries, mutations, and fields, including those not intended for public use.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses schema suggestion errors to brute-force and enumerate additional fields and operations, even if introspection is disabled.
attack_chain.leads_to: Complete or partial reconstruction of the API schema for further exploitation.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends large or complex batch queries to exhaust server resources, causing denial of service.

behavioral_signatures: Error messages with field name suggestions ('Did you mean ...?')
High-frequency or large batch GraphQL requests
Queries with excessive depth or complexity
file_indicators: Log entries with introspection query patterns
Repeated error messages referencing invalid field names
network_indicators: POST requests to /graphql with introspection payloads
Burst of batch GraphQL requests in short timeframes
Unusual error response patterns with schema hints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor GraphQL endpoints for unauthenticated introspection queries, error messages containing field suggestions, and abnormal batch or complex query patterns. Implement rate limiting, query depth/cost analysis, and restrict verbose error messages in production. Alert on repeated schema discovery attempts or DoS-like request patterns.
